question.:question/problem: Suppose $|\,c\,|=18$ and the angle between vectors $c$ and $d$ is $\theta =\frac{3\pi }{4}.$ Find the scalar projection of $c$ onto $d.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{d}\,c & =|\,c\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =18\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{3\pi }{4}) \\  & =18\cdot (-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}) \\  & =-9\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Suppose $|\,a\,|=\frac{19\sqrt{2}}{2}$ and the angle between vectors $a$ and $b$ is $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6}.$ Find the scalar projection of $a$ onto $b.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Using the formula for the scalar projection, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{comp}}_{b}\,a & =|\,a\,|\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\  & =\frac{19\sqrt{2}}{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =\frac{19\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \\  & =\frac{19\sqrt{6}}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
